Q: How left join works with sqlx A:

Here's what I got.

I have a struct like so:

type Posts struct {
    Id            string         `json:"id" db:"posts.id"`
    Uuid          string         `json:"uuid" db:"posts.uuid"`
    Title         string         `json:"title" db:"posts.title"`
    Author        *Users         `json:"author" db:""`
...
}

Which references Users:

type Users struct {
    Id           string         `json:"id" db:"users.id"`
    Name         string         `json:"name" db:"users.name"`
    Slug         string         `json:"slug" db:"users.slug"`
    Email        string         `json:"email" db:"users.email"`
...
}

And then the columns had to be specified with the table names for the select and joins (this is a generic select function meant to work for any query -- the colName is what's important):

func (q *Query[T]) BuildSelectQuery() (err error) {
    var t T

    var table string

    typeOf := reflect.TypeOf(t).String()
    typeOfSplit := strings.Split(typeOf, ".")
    if len(typeOfSplit) > 1 {
        table = strings.ToLower(typeOfSplit[1])
    }

    var cols []string
    for _, c := range q.Columns {
        colName := fmt.Sprintf("%s.%s", table, c)
        cols = append(cols, colName)
    }
...
}

Very important to note if you are using MySQL: the column names being returned by MySQL do not include the table names (i.e., users.id) unless you enable columnsWithAlias in your connection string.

This was the only way to make it work for my use case on MySQL. Otherwise, if there are any ambiguous columns, it won't know what to do.

We are giving sqlx an empty tag for Authors so that it uses the full tag names in Users directly. This made more sense for me than aliasing duplicate columns individually.

If you have no duplicate field names between multiple tables, or if you want to just alias specific columns, you can leave columnsWithAlias off and just treat all of the resulting columns as flat column names that will match up to any nested structs with their tags.

Q: Unambiguously delimited XPath results from xmllint A:

xmllint cannot reliably add delimiters between XPath results because it uses XPath 1.0, which does not support functions like string-join() or iteration over node sets for custom formatting.A better approach is to use xmlstarlet, which allows explicit control over output formatting.

Example:

xmlstarlet sel -t -m "//p" -v . -o "||" input.xml

This will output:

Hello, world!||Bye.||

If you prefer newline-separated results:

xmlstarlet sel -t -m "//p" -v . -n input.xml

Q: gcc undefined reference to gd functions A:

Solved it by changing

gcc -fPIC -O3 -g -O2 -o treeviewer -L/usr/include -lm -lpng -ljpeg -lgd treeviewer.o tree.o fileio.o tree.o

to

gcc -fPIC -O3 -g -O2 treeviewer.o tree.o fileio.o tree.o -L/usr/include -lm -lpng -ljpeg -lgd -o treeviewer

Q: How to remove line breaks from a file in Java? A:

tl;dr

myString.lines().collect( Collectors.joining( "" ) )

Details

You asked two different questions:

  • How to remove line terminators from a string
  • How to remove line terminators from a file

String

The first is incompletely answered by AbstractVoid. Let’s complete that now. We will use the features of modern Java to make simple work of this.

The method String#lines returns a Stream of String objects, one per line within your source string. The following line terminators will have been removed by that method:

  • A line feed character "\n" (U+000A).
  • A carriage return character "\r" (U+000D).
  • A carriage return followed immediately by a line feed "\r\n" (U+000D U+000A).

A stream’s CharSequence (interface of String) elements can be joined together. The result is a single string, just what you desire.

You neglected to mention if you want a new delimiter or not. If not, pass empty string ("").

String joined = myString.lines().collect( Collectors.joining( "" ) ) ;

For example the hard-coded string "a\nb\nc\n" result is “abc”.

File

For your other question, removing line terminators from lines of a file, the solution is quite similar. Use Files.lines to get a Stream of the lines read from the file, and then join.

The stream from the file must be used in try-with-resources syntax to ensure the stream, and its underlying open file, are closed whether the code runs with success or with exception.

Path path = Path.of( "path/to/example.txt" ) ;
try 
        (
                Stream<String> linesStream = Files.lines(path)  // Defaults to UTF-8 character encoding.
        ) 
{
    String joined = linesStream.collect( Collectors.joining( "" ) ) ;
    IO.println( joined ) ;
}

Q: Error Code 0x84BB0001 when installing SQL Server 2016 A:

I realise this is an old post, but I recently struck this issue as I needed to install 2016 for vendor compatibility.

In my case the issue was the service accounts being used.

Solution was to install using the default NT Service virtual accounts then change to domain accounts post install (we were actually using group managed service accounts)

Q: How to use RequestBodyAdvice A:

You should extend WebMvcConfigurationSupport directly for the more specific configuration (instead of @EnableWebMvc if you follow this approach).

Then override this method org.springframework.web.servlet.config.annotation.WebMvcConfigurationSupport#createRequestMappingHandlerAdapter and set your RequestBodyAdvice manually.

This should work

Q: Facebook Graph API - #4 error - application request limit reached A:

App Level Rate Limiting

This rate limiting is applied globally on application level. When the app uses more than allowed resources the error is thrown.

Recommendations:

  • Do not make multiple calls in small amount of time, spread out the calls throughout the day.
  • Do smart fetching of data, you can always fetch important data only, you can remove duplicate data as well
  • Use parameters: "since", "until", "limit" to limit/filter the requests

You can find out more in Official documentation here!
